memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Adam made love to his wife Eve, and she became pregnant and gave birth to Cain. She said, "With the help of the Lord I have brought forth a man." - Gen 4:1 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The very first thing we hear after Eden's gates close is not more judgement, but a birth. Life continues. Eve holds her firstborn and immediately gives credit where it belongs - "with the help of the Lord." Even outside the garden, even under the shadow of the fall, she recognises that this new life came through God's help, not her own strength alone.

There is something tender here. Adam and Eve had lost so much, yet God had not abandoned them. He was still giving, still allowing life to flourish. Eve's words show a heart that is learning to look upward.

For you and me, this is a quiet reminder that God is present in the ordinary beginnings of our lives - a birth, a fresh start, a new season. Nothing good comes to us apart from Him (Jas 1:17). When we pause to say "with the help of the Lord," we are training our hearts to see His hand where we might otherwise see only ourselves.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Where have you forgotten to give God credit lately?
- Do you see God's help in the ordinary parts of your life?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You are present even in life's smallest beginnings. Teach me to say, with Eve, that every good thing comes with Your help.
